game.title: Peele
game.short_description: Build a ladder of three-letter English words to PEE, changing one letter per move and trying to match par.
game.description:
Peele is a daily English word-ladder puzzle with a fixed destination: PEE. Starting from another three-letter word, replace one letter at a time while keeping every step in the game’s dictionary. There is no timer or move limit; a longer valid route still wins.

Daily and practice modes save separately on the current device. Your first daily finish records statistics, while practice lets you try more starts. Par measures a shortest route in this game’s own word list. No account or payment is required.
game.how_to_play: Read the starting word, enter a valid three-letter word with exactly one changed position, and submit it. Repeat from the last accepted word until you reach PEE. Compare accepted moves with par. Rejected entries do not add moves. Use Undo to revisit a branch or Reset to restart the same puzzle.
game.controls: Physical or on-screen keyboard: enter a three-letter word. Enter: submit. Click or tap Undo, Reset, Daily, Practice and New puzzle to use their labeled actions.
game.tips: Work backward from PEE as well as forward from the start. A useful detour may change a letter that already matches the target. Undo unproductive branches instead of repeatedly cycling through the same words. Keep browser storage intact to retain local progress.
game.features: Daily and unlimited practice puzzles; shortest-route par; undo and reset; local progress and statistics; spoiler-free result sharing; physical and on-screen keyboards.

game.title: F1 Reaction Time Test
game.short_description: Wait for five red lights to go out, then react across five valid starts and compare your median, best time and consistency.
game.description:
ReactionMetric’s five-light challenge turns a racing-style start sequence into a short browser reaction game. Five red lights illuminate in sequence; react only after they all switch off. Early inputs count as false starts and the attempt is replayed.

A session needs five valid starts and reports median reaction time, best launch, consistency and false starts. History stays in the current browser. This is an independent entertainment simulation, not an official Formula 1 or FIA timing service; device and display latency affect the measured result.
game.how_to_play: Start a five-start session. Watch the lights and wait through the changing hold after the fifth light. Respond when every light goes out. Repeat until five valid attempts are complete, then review the session results or share a challenge.
game.controls: Click, tap, or press Space to respond after lights out. Use the labeled start, replay and share buttons for session actions.
game.tips: React to the visual change instead of counting down: the hold is randomized. Compare medians on the same device and input method. Treat an unusually fast isolated click cautiously and aim for repeatable starts.
game.features: Five-light visual sequence; randomized hold; false-start tracking; five-valid-start sessions; median, best and consistency results; local history; shareable friend challenges.

researchSources.facts: Official playable HTML, input prompts, five valid starts, false starts replayed, randomized hold, local history, metrics and independent-simulation disclosure.

game.title: Orbital Foundry
game.short_description: Build colonies, research technology and command fleets in a free browser space-strategy alpha; a free account is required for saved gameplay.
game.description:
Orbital Foundry is an early-alpha space-strategy game for modern desktop browsers. Develop colonies around metal, crystal, tritium and energy, expand production and storage, research technologies, and unlock ships. Fleet missions include cargo transport, scouting and timed attacks.

The universe includes other player accounts and six clearly identified computer-controlled factions. English and German are available. A free account is required to play and save progress; the account-free demo is a read-only tour. This is an experimental project seeking testers, with changing balance, bugs and potentially slow initial server loads.
game.how_to_play: Explore the read-only demo first to inspect the interface. For gameplay, open the official site and create a free commander account. Build an economic base, review resource and energy needs, then develop research and ship production. Use the star map and fleet orders to plan transport, scouting or attacks.
game.controls: Use the browser interface’s labeled menus and buttons for infrastructure, economy, research, shipyard, star map and fleet orders. The login screen offers English/German selection.
game.tips: Inspect resource and energy demands before expanding production. Use scouting to gather information before committing fleets. Treat alpha rules and balance as provisional, and report reproducible problems through the linked public project.
game.features: Colony economy and infrastructure; technology research; ship construction; cargo, scout and attack missions; NPC factions and player accounts; English/German interface; account-free read-only demo.

game.title: Galaxy Miner (Space Clicker)
game.short_description: Mine Stardust, balance Heat Flux, buy automatic producers and reset for lasting Dark Matter upgrades in a browser space clicker.
game.description:
Galaxy Miner is the flagship incremental game on SpaceClickerGame.com. Begin by mining Stardust manually, then reinvest in tools and automatic producers such as drones, rovers, bases and orbital stations. As production grows, planet milestones and permanent progression take over more of the work.

Manual mining raises Heat. Staying in the 80–99% Heat Flux band doubles active output, while overheating temporarily interrupts mining. Galactic Reset unlocks at one trillion Stardust and exchanges the current run for Dark Matter progression. Saves are local, with portable backup options and capped offline-production credit.
game.how_to_play: Open Galaxy Miner rather than one of the site’s separate simulations. Mine Stardust, purchase affordable output upgrades and add automation. Manage Heat while building toward planet thresholds. When Galactic Reset becomes available, review the displayed Dark Matter gain before resetting the run.
game.controls: Click or tap the mining control. Desktop: Space mines; 1–8 quick-buy standard upgrade tiers; P toggles the prestige chamber; S opens Telemetry & Backup; M toggles audio; H or ? opens hotkey help. Gameplay shortcuts do not intercept text entered into focused form fields.
game.tips: Use short bursts to benefit from Heat Flux without overheating. Compare an upgrade’s payback with the next planet milestone. Review permanent reset gains before discarding a productive run. Export a backup before clearing browser storage or moving devices.
game.features: Manual mining and automated production; Heat Flux timing; planet multipliers; Dark Matter prestige; permanent Void Technology; capped offline production; local saves with portable export/import; desktop hotkeys and touch controls.

game.title: Schätz mal!
game.short_description: Answer five German estimation questions by entering a number and comparing it with the real value.
game.description:
